title: Kernel Curator: online autotuner for architecture + sequence-length bucketed kernel selection
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: implement a runtime component (Kernel Curator) that continuously recommends and safely rolls out micro-kernel choices per model serving path based on hardware architecture and sequence-length buckets. The curator must balance tail latency SLOs, throughput, and per-token compute cost. It should use a mix of offline microbenchmarks, warm-start priors, and lightweight online probing with bounded risk (probe budget + rollback). The outcome should reduce per-token cost for mixed workloads while preserving p95/p99 latency targets and providing explainability to operators.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits kernel_choice events and probe metrics to metrics pipeline
Can configure seqlen_buckets and exploration_budget in model manifest
Show per-route cost/latency delta on Console for a canary rollout
Automatic rollback to safe kernel if p99 increases > 10% over baseline for 5 minutes
End-to-end e2e job demonstrates >=5% token-cost reduction on at least one mixed workload trace without violating latency SLO
tasks: Design offline microbenchmark schema (arch x kernel x seqlen buckets)
Implement Kernel Curator service and runtime hooks for nondisruptive probes
Add model-manifest config fields: seqlen_buckets, preferred_kernels, exploration_budget, latency_slo_ms, cost_weight
Integrate probe metrics into Console dashboards and rollout API
Create staged rollout plan + canary tooling and automatic rollback policy
Add synthetic workload and chaos tests to CI
notes: Motivation: existing kernel choice is static or heuristic-driven and fails to capture workload shifts in seqlen distribution, costing us tokens on average and causing occasional p99 regressions on spikes.
Prior art consulted: bandit-based online selectors (Thompson sampling with safety constraints), p99-aware regularized reward functions, per-architecture kernel catalogs maintained by infra team.
initial_spike_results: Microbenchmarks on A100 vs H100 show different knee points: A100 prefers kernel-X for seqlen <= 128, H100 prefers kernel-Y up to 256 for same batch sizes
A warm-start prior from offline corpus reduces exploration cost by ~60% in simulation
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal staging traffic with exploration_budget=0.02 and canary route (5% traffic)
Phase 2: Safety window monitoring with p95/p99 and cost signals for 24h; if stable, increase to 20%
Phase 3: Gradual global rollout with automated rollback triggers and human notification
qa_plan: Synthetic traces: short, medium, long seqlen mixes; verify p99 and cost movement
Chaos test: temporarily reduce GPU availability to force fallbacks and verify curator picks safe kernels
A/B: compare canary vs baseline for 72h and report token-cost and latency distributions
open_blockers: Telemetry sampling rate for kernel probe metrics must be increased (PM/Observability ticket filed)
Need additional QPS on microbenchmark infra to generate warm-start priors for some older instance types
